hypothesis: A conventional 32x33 padded shared tile with 32x8 threads should preserve coalesced input loads and output stores while avoiding the XOR indexing of the prior 32x32 swizzled variant. The prior variant was correct and measured substantially faster than the naive baseline, but it does not establish whether padding or XOR indexing performs better on this target; this candidate provides the contrasting layout for that measurement.
notes: This proposal has not been built or measured in this turn. Existing evidence: the baseline built and passed all eight cases; its n=1024 samples were 17.13376, 16.74880, and 16.87456 microseconds (mean 16.91904). The prior XOR-swizzled candidate built and passed all eight cases; its samples were 3.34272, 3.20192, and 3.21568 microseconds (mean 3.25344). Controller build, correctness, and repeated timing results are needed for the padded candidate and a direct comparison.
transformations: Replace the naive transpose launch with a single-pass 32x32 shared-memory tiled transpose using a 32x8 block; each thread handles four rows.
Use a padded 32x33 scalar shared tile, load each tile row coalesced, synchronize, and store with tile axes exchanged so output rows are coalesced.
Preserve the run entry point and copy float values without arithmetic or additional allocation.
